frozen_controls_to_retain.normalization: For each example, sum active supervised-token terms divided by ALL its active-token count, then average examples. Never divide by the sum of probability weights; never substitute a global token mean.
frozen_controls_to_retain.causal_alignment: Exactly one external shift: normalized backbone state at position t predicts the unchanged label at t+1. Mask -100 exactly once. The native EOS and every supervised terminal-tail token remain in loss and diagnostics.
frozen_controls_to_retain.headroom_formula: total - (max(whole_allocated_peak, whole_reserved_peak) + sampled_nonallocator_peak) >= max(16 * 2**30, ceil(0.1 * total))

recommended_checkpointed_head_design.model_boundary: Use the pinned Qwen2 backbone's final normalized hidden states and the SAME original lm_head module/Parameter. A new explicit wrapper may return only the scalar loss and detached bounded metrics to the prepared Trainer; it must not return all logits for Accelerate to recursively convert to FP32. Do not modify upstream libraries, old modules or global forward/loss mappings.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.tied_weight_identity: The pinned model ties input embeddings and output projection. Preserve the original alias/storage and all434 unique trainable parameter tensors. Do not clone, detach, freeze or independently optimize the head. Dense-vs-chunk gradient checks must include the combined embedding-plus-head gradient.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.backbone_passes: Student backbone retains the same training/gradient-checkpointing/SDPA/mask/position/RoPE/cache-disabled behavior. Reference backbone is a separate eval-mode FP32-storage frozen model under the same BF16 autocast and torch.no_grad, producing normal detached hidden tensors rather than inference tensors.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.chunk_schedule: Retain contiguous 128 causally aligned sequence-position windows to match the existing chunk boundary policy. Validate labels/masks and finite hidden values before selecting the active rows of a window. Windows with no supervised targets contribute no objective term. No sequence, label or response may be changed.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.checkpoint_boundary: Put the student head projection AND FP32 full-vocabulary log_softmax/objective in one non-reentrant checkpoint region with explicit immutable inputs and use_reentrant=false. Project the matching detached reference hidden chunk with the frozen reference head inside that bounded region under no_grad. Do not precompute or retain complete student/reference logits, probabilities or log-probabilities outside it.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.exact_objective: For each active position use CE=-log p(target), forward KL=sum_v q_v*(log q_v-log p_v), and detached weight1 for SFT/CE+KL, detached p(target) for ASFT, or detached q(target) for prior anchoring. Full vocabulary is151936; no top-k, chosen-token KL, temperature alteration, probability clipping or approximate distillation is allowed.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.metrics: Return detached per-chunk sums/counts only, including actual EOS-ID and complementary non-EOS totals computed from the same chunk terms. Do not retain per-vocabulary tensors for metrics or run a second full head solely for diagnostics. No metrics or reference inputs may carry autograd graphs.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.autograd: Retain one differentiable normalized scalar for the ordinary Trainer backward. Do not add manual per-chunk backward, manual gradient-accumulation scaling, alternate optimizer steps or hidden detached-gradient injection in this first design. Checkpoint closures must not capture a later loop iteration's mutable state. Preserve autocast configuration on recomputation and declare RNG policy explicitly.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.numerical_qualification: This preserves the mathematical objective, not assumed bitwise equality. Smaller BF16 GEMMs, changed summation order and checkpoint recomputation can change rounding. Freeze loss/logit/gradient/update tolerances prospectively using the existing native parity standard plus an independently reviewed gradient/update criterion; never relax a gate after observing a failure.
recommended_checkpointed_head_design.cost: Up to249 head windows on the current longest input, plus head/objective recomputation during backward and potentially frozen-head recomputation. Smaller GEMMs and per-chunk validation can reduce throughput. There is no measured speedup or guaranteed fit; a fixed finite engineering allocation must measure actual wall time and all phases. This keeps one GPU per wall hour and avoids distributed collectives/global-batch changes.

two_b200_full_shard_comparison.credible_benefit: FSDP2 can shard student FP32 parameters, gradients and two FP32 Adam moments. The ideal persistent-storage saving is24.69GB per rank before transient costs. Replicating the separate frozen FP32 reference leaves its12.34GB parameter storage per rank; sharding that reference would be an additional separately tested choice.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.remaining_problem: FSDP is data parallel parameter sharding, not token/vocabulary activation sharding: each rank still materializes its own full local LxV output under the current forward. Layerwise all-gathers, backward reduce-scatter, prefetch and communication buffers add peaks; two B200s do not guarantee the unchanged full-logit path passes headroom.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.precision_control: To preserve FP32 parameter storage and existing op-level BF16 autocast, use original-dtype unsharded parameters (MixedPrecisionPolicy.param_dtype=None) and explicit FP32 reduction, subject to native proof. Setting FSDP param_dtype=bfloat16 applies module-level compute precision and cannot silently be called identical to the current FP32-parameter autocast path.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.accumulation_control: Pinned FSDP2 no_sync can retain unsharded accumulated gradients. Do not claim ideal gradient sharding while disabling synchronization across the group. Synchronizing/reduce-scattering every microbatch can retain sharded accumulation at extra communication cost and needs independent FP32 scaling/finite-norm tests.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.exposure_control: Two ranks each consuming microbatch1 with GA8 makes global batch16. Preserving the former global batch8 requires an explicit two-rank GA4 or another prospectively sealed schedule, including exact record order, equal-example weighting and uneven final-group handling. Duplicating the same row on both ranks can be a diagnostic parity control but doubles work without sharding local activations.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.new_evidence_required: The current Trainer rejects FSDP/multiple processes. A distributed runner would require new DTensor optimizer membership, globally correct clipping/finite moments, reference exclusion, tied weights, rank-specific receipt/completion rules, collective failure handling, full checkpoint consolidation/reload and consumed-example proofs. Existing single-GPU434-state/headroom receipts cannot certify it.
two_b200_full_shard_comparison.cost_and_decision: Two concurrent B200s consume two GPU-hours per wall hour plus communication/queue costs. They could improve throughput on distinct examples but no speedup is measured. This is a credible later fallback after an explicit redesign, not the smallest next bounded step for the observed full-logit allocation problem.

The original forward uses the final normalized backbone state, then a separate bias-free linear head. This supports a new explicit head-scheduling wrapper without changing decoder math; its numerical equivalence still needs testing.

locations: native AMP forward wrapping around lines1633-1644
primary_sources.evidence: Prepared native-AMP model forwards are wrapped with recursive FP32 output conversion.
BF16/FP16 tensor outputs in nested structures are converted to FP32. Returning full logits therefore matters even when the original head computes BF16.

Checkpointing trades recomputation for saved-activation memory; non-reentrant mode is recommended. A changed forward/recompute invocation can silently give incorrect gradients, so explicit state/RNG and parity controls are necessary.
Pinned checkpoint implementation captures autocast settings and re-enters them during recomputation. This is source support, not proof the proposed closure is correct.
FSDP2 uses per-parameter DTensor sharding, all-gather/reduce-scatter hooks, bottom-up grouping and DTensor optimizer state. Full state dict consolidation differs from a single-GPU save.
param_dtype controls unsharded forward/backward/all-gather precision; original-dtype sharded parameters serve the optimizer. reduce_dtype also controls unsynchronized accumulation dtype.
Without reduction, accumulated gradients remain unsharded before later reduce-scatter; no_sync is not the ideal sharded-gradient memory envelope.
The pinned Trainer scales by actual current accumulation-group length for the declared loss contract. A chunked scalar must not add a second manual accumulation division.
